4291.new_note: *And behold the heavens were opened, and an angel of Elohim (God) said to me, Levi, enter.* Levi, telling his sons of his vision (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 18:6), names the heavens-opening at the priestly investiture — the same heavens-opening Matt 3:16 narrates over Yahusha (Jesus) at the Yarden (Jordan). The Hebrew library knew the heavens open at the moment a covenant-bearing figure is invested for service; the gospel's opening of the heavens follows the same architecture.

4291.old_note: *And behold the heavens were opened, and an angel of Elohim (God) said to me, Levi, enter.* Testament of Levi 2:6 (TestXII ch 12:6 in the Charles concatenation) names the heavens-opening at the priestly investiture — the same heavens-opening Matt 3:16 narrates over Yahusha (Jesus) at the Yarden (Jordan). 4315.new_note: *Again, the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain, and sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;* (Matthew 4:8). *After it is consummated, Beliar the great ruler, the king of this world, will descend, who hath ruled it since it came into being; yea, he will descent from his firmament in the likeness of a man, a lawless king, the slayer of his mother: who himself (even) this king.* (Ascension of Isaiah 4:2). The Ascension of Isaiah says that Beliar is the king of this world and has ruled it since it came into being. When the devil takes Yahusha (Jesus) up the mountain and shows him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory, he is showing what he holds for the present age, so the offer that follows was no empty boast. But the same passage speaks of the completion of the world, and a rule that was given for a season is a rule with an end.
4315.member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 4:2 — *Beliar the great ruler, the king of this world, will descend, who hath ruled it since it came into being.* The Ascension of Isaiah names the one who has ruled this world from the beginning, and the devil offers Yahusha (Jesus) what he holds.
4315.reason: Live text of 4:2 carries a misprint, 'he will descent' (for 'descend'); quoted exactly as it stands. Old note quoted a different wording of the verse than the live text and used the phrases 'the Hebrew library' and 'Watcher-rebellion administration', which I dropped.
4315.old_note: *And after it is consummated, Beliar will descend, the great angel, the king of this world, which he has ruled ever since it came into being; and he will descend from his firmament in the form of a man, a king of unrighteousness, a slayer of his mother — this is the king of this world.* Ascension of Isaiah 4:2 names Beliar as *the king of this world,* the figure who has ruled it from the beginning. Matt 4:8-9's offer of *all the kingdoms of the world* by the devil is the same king-of-this-world figure offering what he currently administers. The Hebrew library's framework — Beliar / the devil as the temporary king-of-this-world during the present age (under Watcher-rebellion administration) — locks the framework reading that the wilderness-offer was not an empty bluff.

4316.new_note: *And saith unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.* (Matthew 4:9). *And they will sacrifice to him and they will serve him saying: "This is Elohim (God) and beside him there is no other." And they greater number of those who shall have been associated together in order to receive the Beloved, he will turn aside after him.* (Ascension of Isaiah 4:8–9). Satan asks Yahusha (Jesus) for worship, and Yahusha (Jesus) refuses. The Ascension of Isaiah shows what the same ruler gets from the world in the days of the end: sacrifice and service, and the cry that there is no other god beside him, and then the greater number of those gathered to receive the Beloved turned aside after him. It is the same grab for worship, once refused by the Son in the wilderness, and then carried out on the many who do not hold fast.
4316.member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 4:9 — *those who shall have been associated together in order to receive the Beloved, he will turn aside after him.* The ruler who asked the Son for worship turns aside the greater number of those gathered to receive the Beloved.
4316.reason: Live text of 4:9 has a misprint, 'And they greater number' (for 'the'); quoted exactly. I quoted 4:8 with it because the worship the verse is about is in 4:8. Old note quoted wording from earlier in chapter 4 (the ruler speaking as the Beloved and saying he is Elohim), not 4:9; I kept its point (the worship grab) and anchored it on what 4:8 to 4:9 says.
4316.old_note: *And much power will be in his hands, and he will make all do what he chooses; and he will speak as the Beloved and will say: I am Elohim (God), and before me there was none. And all the people in the world will believe in him.* Ascension 4:9 names Beliar's standing worship-grab pattern — speaking as the Beloved, claiming the worship due to Elohim. Matt 4:9's *if thou wilt fall down and worship me* is the king-of-this-world enacting the same worship-grab at the Messianic level. The Hebrew library names the architecture; the gospel narrates one instance of it.

4317.new_note: *Then saith Yahusha (Jesus) unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God), and him only shalt thou serve.* (Matthew 4:10). *For Beliar was in great wrath against Isaiah by reason of the vision, and because of the exposure wherewith he had exposed Sammael, and because through him the going forth of the Beloved from the seventh heaven had been made known, and His transformation and His descent and the likeness into which He should be transformed (that is) the likeness of man, and the persecution wherewith he should be persecuted, and the torturers wherewith the children of Yashar'el (Israel) should torture Him, and the coming of His twelve disciples, and the teaching, and that He should before the sabbath be crucified upon the tree, and should be crucified together with wicked men, and that He should be buried in the sepulchre,* (Ascension of Isaiah 3:13). Beliar's rage against Isaiah is over one thing: the prophet had made known the Beloved's going forth from the seventh heaven and his descent in the likeness of man. In the wilderness the same adversary meets the Beloved now come down in that likeness, and is sent away with the commandment of Torah: worship Yahuah (the Lord) and serve him only. The one Beliar tried to keep hidden dismisses him with the Word.
4317.member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 3:13 — *the going forth of the Beloved from the seventh heaven had been made known.* The Beloved whose descent enraged Beliar sends Satan away with the Torah's own word.
4317.reason: Re-pointed from 1:3 to 3:13 — the verse the old note quoted (Beliar's wrath at the revealing of the Beloved); 1:3 is the list of judgments and powers. Live 3:13 text is long and is quoted whole, as the rule requires.
4317.old_note: *Beliar was wroth with Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) because of his vision, and because of the unmasking with which he had unmasked Sammael, and because by him the going forth of the Beloved from the seventh heaven had been made known.* Ascension 1:3 names Beliar's adversarial pattern toward the prophetic revelation of the Beloved's descent. Matt 4:10's *Get thee hence, Satan* sends the same Beliar-figure away in the same architecture: the Beloved who has descended dismisses the king-of-this-world who opposes the descent.

4339.new_note: *But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.* (Matthew 5:22). *For in the presence of my father I spake peaceably to Joseph; and when I had gone out, the spirit of hatred darkened my mind, and stirred up my soul to slay him.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:2). Gad is speaking to his sons about what he did to Joseph. In front of their father he spoke peaceably, and the moment he had gone out hatred darkened his mind and drove his soul toward killing his brother. That is the road Yahusha (Jesus) is describing: the commandment against murder was never only about the hand, because anger at a brother is where the killing begins. He is not setting the Torah aside but reading the commandment down to its root, the same root Gad learned the hard way and warned his children about.
4339.member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:2 — *the spirit of hatred darkened my mind, and stirred up my soul to slay him.* Gad confesses that hatred began as a darkened mind and ended in a plan to kill, which is the very path Yahusha (Jesus) traces back to anger.
4339.reason: Old citation (Testament of Gad 2:2) was stale; card sits on the right verse, now cited by the live numbering. Old note quoted the previous verse inside the italics; I quote only 100:2.
4339.old_note: *Love one another in deed, and in word, and in the inclination of the soul. For in the presence of my father I spake peaceably to Joseph; and when I had gone out, the spirit of hatred darkened my mind, and stirred up my soul to slay him.* Testament of Gad 2:2 (DB ch 62) names the spirit-of-hatred-to-the-act-of-murder architecture in the patriarch's own testimony — the heart-root that the Torah always taught the murder-commandment named. Matt 5:22's *whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment* walks the same Hebrew library architecture at the antithesis-restoration level: the oral tradition stopped at the bodily act; the Torah and the testaments and the Beatitudes name the heart-substance the act follows from.

4341.new_note: *But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;* (Matthew 5:44). *Love ye one another from the heart; and if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile; and if he repent and confess, forgive him.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3). Gad does not stop at loving the brother who treats you well. If a man sins against you, speak peaceably to him, keep no guile in your soul, and forgive him when he repents. Yahusha (Jesus) reaches the same place from the other side, telling us to bless those who curse us, do good to those who hate us, and pray for those who persecute us. This is not a teaching set against Moses; the fathers were already handing it to their sons, and Gad hands it down out of what hatred did to Joseph.
4341.member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3 — *if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile.* Gad tells his sons to answer a brother's wrong with peace and forgiveness, which is the same heart Yahusha (Jesus) asks for toward an enemy.
4341.reason: Old note quoted 'cast forth the poison of hate', which is not in the live 100:3 (the poison language belongs to the next verse, 100:4); I quote only what 100:3 says. Citation moved from stale 'Gad 2:3' to live 100:3.
4341.old_note: *Love ye one another from the heart; and if a man sin against thee, cast forth the poison of hate and speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile.* Testament of Gad 2:3 (DB ch 62) names the love-replacing-hatred ethic at the heart level — *cast forth the poison of hate and speak peaceably.* Matt 5:44's *love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you* walks the same Hebrew library ethic at the Sermon level. The antithesis is not a Yahusha (Jesus) innovation against Mosheh (Moses); the love-of-the-personal-enemy ethic was already taught in the patriarch's own testimony to his sons.

4427.new_note: *Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;* (Matthew 9:37). *Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.* (2 Baruch 70:2). Baruch looks ahead to the time when the age has ripened and the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, and the Mighty One brings bewilderment on the earth and its rulers. Yahusha (Jesus), looking at the crowds, says the harvest truly is plenteous, and the labourers are few. What Baruch placed at the end of the age, Yahusha (Jesus) says is already at hand. Both speak of a harvest of two kinds of seed, which is why the sorting matters and why labourers are wanted.
4427.member_note: 2 Baruch 70:2 — *the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come.* The harvest of the age, evil and good seeds together, is the harvest Yahusha (Jesus) says is already plenteous.
4427.reason: Old note cited 2 Baruch 35:1 (stale numbering); the quoted words are in the live 2 Baruch 70:2, and the card sits on 70:2. The 'good and evil seeds' read as the two kinds sown together until harvest; no further claim made.
4427.old_note: *Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon them...* 2 Baruch 35:1 names the wisdom-stream's apocalyptic-harvest architecture explicitly — the harvest comes when the time of the age has ripened; the harvest is of evil-and-good-seeds together. Matt 9:37's *the harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few* walks the same architecture at the King's arrival: the harvest the apocalyptic-stream had named as eschatologically-future is now plenteous and present at the King's seeing of the multitudes.

4428.new_note: *Pray ye therefore Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.* (Matthew 9:38) *Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.* (2 Baruch 70:2) Yahusha (Jesus) sees the crowds and tells his disciples to ask Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest for labourers, because the harvest is standing ready. Baruch had already been told what that harvest is: the time of the age ripens, and what was sown in it, evil seed and good seed alike, has come up. The one Baruch calls the Mighty One is the owner of that field, so the prayer in Matthew is a prayer prayed inside that ripening time, and the next chapter sends the twelve out as the answer.
4428.member_note: 2 Baruch 70:2 — *the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come.* The prayer Yahusha (Jesus) teaches in Matthew 9:38 asks for workers for this same harvest.

4428.old_note: *Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon them...* 2 Baruch 35:1 — the same eschatological-harvest-of-the-age verse also anchors Matt 9:38's *pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers.* The Lord-of-the-harvest is the Mighty One the apocalyptic-stream had named; the labourers being prayed-for are about to be commissioned at Matt 10:1.

4431.new_note: *But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.* (Matthew 9:36) *And truly I know that behold all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.* (2 Baruch 78:3) Yahusha (Jesus) looks at the multitudes and finds them scattered and without a shepherd, which is a picture of a people and not of a crowd of strangers. Baruch writes to the brethren in captivity and says who that people is: the twelve tribes, bound by one bond because they are born from one father. However far they have been carried, they are one flock by birth, and that is what moves Yahusha (Jesus) to compassion.
4431.member_note: 2 Baruch 78:3 — *all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.* The scattered, shepherdless multitudes Yahusha (Jesus) sees in Matthew 9:36 are this one family born from one father.
4431.reason: Old note cited 2 Baruch 38:4 (stale numbering); fixed to the live 78:3.
4431.old_note: *And truly I know that behold all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.* 2 Baruch 38:4 names the twelve-tribes-bound-by-one-bond architecture in the wisdom-stream's apocalyptic register — all the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, born from one father. The framework's gathering-thesis holds the twelve-tribe-restoration as the load-bearing prophetic substance; Matt 9:36's *sheep having no shepherd* multitudes are the same twelve-tribe-bound-by-one-bond body the wisdom-stream had named.

4432.new_note: *But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.* (Matthew 9:36) *For if ye so do these things, He will continually remember you, He who always promised on our behalf to those who were more excellent than we, that He will never forget or forsake us, but with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.* (2 Baruch 78:7) Yahusha (Jesus) is moved with compassion at sheep scattered abroad with no shepherd. Baruch closes his letter to the scattered tribes with the promise that answers it: Yahuah (Lord) will never forget or forsake them, and with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed. The compassion in Matthew and the mercy in Baruch are one mercy, and its work is the gathering.
4432.member_note: 2 Baruch 78:7 — *with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.* The compassion Yahusha (Jesus) shows the scattered sheep in Matthew 9:36 is this promised mercy at work.
4432.reason: Old note cited 2 Baruch 38:7 (stale numbering) and tied it to Hosea 6:6 at Matthew 9:13; I dropped the Hosea link because no live text for it was given to quote. Citation fixed to 78:7.
4432.old_note: *He who always promised on our behalf to those who were more excellent than we, that He will never forget or forsake us, but with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.* 2 Baruch 38:7 (epistle to the nine-and-a-half scattered tribes across the Euphrates) names the wisdom-stream's gathering-of-the-dispersed-with-much-mercy architecture explicitly. The much-mercy register at 2 Baruch 38:7 is the same mercy-substance Hosea 6:6 names at Matt 9:13; the gathering-of-the-dispersed IS the mercy-architecture of the kingdom-at-hand.

4457.new_note: *Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.* (Matthew 10:4). *Will persecute the plant which the Twelve Apostles of the Beloved have planted. Of the Twelve one will be delivered into his hands.* (Ascension of Isaiah 4:3). Before the Twelve are ever named, the Ascension of Isaiah says that the ruler of this world will persecute what they plant and that one of the Twelve will fall into his hands. Matthew's list of the apostles closes on exactly that note, with the last name carrying the word betrayed. Nothing in the account takes the Beloved by surprise. The persecution of the plant and the loss of one from the inner circle were spoken of ahead of time, and Matthew's commissioning of the Twelve goes on to warn them of what is coming.
4457.member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 4:3 — *Of the Twelve one will be delivered into his hands.* The persecution of the plant and the loss of one of the Twelve were told in advance, and Matthew's list ends on the one who betrayed.
4457.reason: Old note's phrase list (wisdom-stream, architecture elements) removed. 4:3 begins mid-sentence in the live text ('Will persecute...'); its subject is the ruler of 4:2.
4457.old_note: *Will persecute the plant which the Twelve Apostles of the Beloved have planted. Of the Twelve one will be delivered into his hands.* The Ascension of Isaiah 4:3 (in the Belial-prediction at the chapter's mid-section) names the wisdom-stream's prophetic-witness to the twelve-apostles-with-one-betrayer architecture explicitly — the plant the Twelve plant will be persecuted; one of the Twelve will be delivered into the hand of the persecutor. Matt 10:4's Yahudah (Judah) Iscariot listed-with-betrayal-note and Matt 10:16-22's persecution-disclosure walk the same architecture at the commissioning-discourse register. The framework reads the Ascension passage as the wisdom-stream's confirmation that the inner-circle-betrayal and the persecution-of-the-plant are not surprise-developments but architecture-elements named in advance.

4695.new_note: *So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.* (Matthew 18:35). *Love ye one another from the heart; and if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile; and if he repent and confess, forgive him.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3). Yahusha (Jesus) closes His warning with the words from your hearts: the Father will deal with us as we deal with a brother we will not forgive. Gad gives his sons the same measure. Love one another from the heart, speak peaceably to a brother who sins against you, and when he repents and confesses, forgive him. Both put the whole matter in the heart, where a brother is either forgiven or kept in the ledger.
4695.member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3 — *Love ye one another from the heart.* Gad's call to love from the heart and forgive the repentant brother stands behind the warning that closes Yahusha's (Jesus's) teaching on forgiveness.
4695.reason: Old note cited stale 'Testament of Gad 62:3' and leaned on Matthew 18:15-17 and the unforgiving-servant parable, neither of which is on this card; I kept the one true link (from the heart, forgive the brother) and cited by live numbering.
4695.old_note: *Love ye one another from the heart; and if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him.* Testament of Gad 62:3 names the wisdom-stream's articulation of the heart-substance + the speak-peaceably-to-the-sinning-brother substance the King's chapter-arc lands-on at v.35 and operationalizes at vv.15-17. The framework reads the verse against the unforgiving-servant parable + the assembly-discipline procedure. The Testament-of-Gad's confessional-instruction — Gad confessing his-own-hatred-of-Joseph and the substance-of-repentance he-came-to — names the heart-substance the King's *from your hearts* (v.35) requires. The framework reads this as the wisdom-stream's direct prefiguring of both ends of the chapter-arc: (a) the v.15 first-step *go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone* operates from the substance Testament of Gad names — *speak peaceably to him*; (b) the v.35 chapter-closing *if ye from your hearts forgive not* operates from the substance Testament of Gad names — *love ye one another from the heart.* The wisdom-stream had carried the heart-substance; the King's assembly-architecture institutionalizes the heart-substance at the kingdom-citizens' corporate-register.

4710.new_note: *Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.* (Matthew 19:21) *Work righteousness, therefore, my children, upon the earth, That ye may have (it) as a treasure in heaven.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 29:5) Yahusha (Jesus) tells the rich young man that if he wants to be perfect he should go, sell what he has, give to the poor, and have treasure in heaven, and then come and follow. Levi tells his sons the same thing in other words: work righteousness on the earth, and it is kept as a treasure in heaven. Just before this, Yahusha (Jesus) had told the man that the way into life is to keep the commandments, so the treasure in heaven is what righteousness done on the earth is laid up as.
4710.member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 29:5 — *Work righteousness, therefore, my children, upon the earth, That ye may have (it) as a treasure in heaven.* Levi's call to work righteousness on the earth and have it as a treasure in heaven is the word Yahusha (Jesus) speaks in Matthew 19:21.
4710.reason: Old note cited this as Levi 7 verse 5 / chapter 18 (stale); fixed to 29:5. Also tied to 1 Timothy 6:18–19; dropped since no live text was given to quote.
4710.old_note: *Work righteousness, therefore, my children, upon the earth, that ye may have it as a treasure in heaven.* Testaments XII Levi 7 (chapter 18 in the corpus enumeration) verse 5 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the *treasure in heaven* substance — the exact phrase the King restates at Matt 19:21's *thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.* The framework reads this as the wisdom-stream's most-direct verbal-prefiguration of the King's-substance. The Levi-testament-substance had named the architecture: *work righteousness... that ye may have it as a treasure in heaven.* The kingdom-citizens' substance is righteousness-walked-on-the-earth that-translates-into-treasure-in-heaven; the substance is in continuity with the apostolic-restatement at 1 Timothy 6:18-19's *that they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate; laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come.* The King at Matt 19:21 stands on the wisdom-stream-substance the Test XII Levi 7 had named. The framework reads this in continuity with the FRAMEWORK-MAJOR substance the King ties to the kingdom-entry-criterion at v.17 — *keep the commandments* — and the diagnostic-test at v.21 the heart-Torah-substance lands on. The wisdom-stream, the King, and the apostle all hold the same substance: righteousness-walked + treasure-in-heaven are one architecture.

4720.new_note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28). *There were twelve harts feeding: and the nine were (first) dispersed over all the earth, and likewise also the three.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 129:2). Joseph sees twelve harts feeding together, and all twelve end up dispersed over the earth, the nine first and the three likewise. The twelve harts read as the twelve tribes, scattered. Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of those same tribes as a whole people sitting under judgment when the Son of Adam takes His throne, with twelve thrones set for judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel). A people who are to be judged as twelve tribes must first be gathered as twelve, and Joseph's vision is the scattering that the gathering answers.
4720.member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 129:2 — *There were twelve harts feeding: and the nine were (first) dispersed over all the earth.* Joseph's vision of twelve harts dispersed over the earth is the scattering that Yahusha (Jesus) assumes when He speaks of judging the twelve tribes.
4720.reason: Old note said the nine are the ten northern tribes and the three are the southern house. Nine is not ten and three is not two, so I did not carry that identification; I say only what the verse says (twelve dispersed, nine first, then the three). Old citation ('Joseph 15', 'chapter 86') was stale; live 129:2 used.
4720.old_note: *There were twelve harts feeding: and the nine were (first) dispersed over all the earth, and likewise also the three.* Testaments XII Joseph 15 (chapter 86 in the corpus enumeration) verse 2 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the twelve-harts-feeding-then-dispersed substance — the same scattering-and-restoration-of-the-twelve-tribes architecture the King at Matt 19:28's *judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)* presupposes-as-the-completed-gathering-architecture. The framework reads the verse against the King's-statement. The Joseph-testament-substance names the substance directly: twelve-harts (the twelve-tribes) feeding-together-originally, then-dispersed (the nine = the ten-northern-tribes; the three = the southern-house-substance), the substance the prophets had named at Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 37:15-22's two-sticks-becoming-one. The substance the King-states at Matt 19:28 is the gathering-and-judging-substance the wisdom-stream-Joseph-testament had named the architecture-for. The wisdom-stream, the Tanakh-prophets, and the King's-mouth all hold the same architecture: twelve-tribes-dispersed-and-gathered-and-judged-by-twelve-apostles-at-the-consummated-substance. The framework reads in framework-substance per Red Line #11 — the twelve-tribes are LITERAL twelve-tribes, the paternal-blood remnant the Father-promised-through-the-prophets-and-now-states-at-the-King's-mouth. FRAMEWORK-MAJOR.

4737.new_note: *Even as the Son of Adam came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.* (Matthew 20:28). *And He shall ascend from Hades and shall pass from earth into heaven. 4826.new_note: *And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* (Matthew 24:30). *Until the El Elyon (Most High) shall visit the earth, coming Himself [as man, with men eating and drinking], and breaking the head of the dragon in the water. He shall save Yashar'el (Israel) and all the Gentiles [Elohim (God) speaking in the person of man].* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 109:3). Asher has just told his sons that they will sin, be handed to their enemies, and be scattered to the four corners of the earth. Then he says the Most High will visit the earth, coming Himself as man, and will save Yashar'el (Israel) and the Gentiles, who stand right beside the scattered of the verse before. Matthew shows the same one at the end of that road, the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven, all the tribes of the earth mourning, and the Son of Adam coming in the clouds with power and great glory. The one who comes in the person of man is Yahusha (Jesus), the one in whom Elohim (God) took form, who walked with Adam's line from the beginning and came in flesh, and the tribes that mourn are the tribes Asher says were scattered.

4861.new_note: *Then saith Yahusha (Jesus) unto them, All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad.* (Matthew 26:31) *And behold, I am clear from your ungodliness and transgression, which ye shall commit in the end of the ages [against the Saviour of the world, Messiah (Christ), acting godlessly], deceiving Yashar'el (Israel), and stirring up against it great evils from Yahuah (Lord).* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 26:2) On the night of his arrest Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples they will all be offended because of him, and says it is written that the shepherd will be smitten and the sheep scattered. Long before, Levi told his sons that at the end of the ages they would act ungodly against the Saviour of the world, deceiving Yashar'el (Israel) and leaving it open to great evils. Both describe leadership failing and the flock scattered as a result. The one who is smitten was himself born of Yahudah (Judah) and came for his people, so what is named here is a corrupt leadership, not the people.

4862.new_note: *Then the high priest rent his clothes, saying, He hath spoken blasphemy; what further need have we of witnesses? behold, now ye have heard his blasphemy.* (Matthew 26:65) *And ye shall deal lawlessly together with Yashar'el (Israel), so He shall not bear with Jerusalem because of your wickedness; but the veil of the temple shall be rent, so as not to cover your shame.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 26:3) The high priest tears his own clothes and calls the truth blasphemy, though the Torah forbids the high priest to rend his clothes. Levi had said that when the lawlessness of the leaders of his line was full, it would be the veil of the temple that was rent, so as not to cover their shame. 4863.new_note: *For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.* (Matthew 26:28). *In thee shall be fulfilled the prophecy of heaven [concerning the Lamb of Elohim (God), and Saviour of the world], that a blameless one shall be delivered up for lawless men, and a sinless shall die for ungodly men [in the blood of the covenant, for the salvation of the Gentiles and 'of Israel', and shall destroy Beliar and his servants].* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 133:8). Jacob, embracing Joseph, tells him that in him the prophecy of heaven will be fulfilled: a blameless one delivered up for lawless men, a sinless one dying for ungodly men in the blood of the covenant. Yahusha (Jesus) at the table gives that blood its name, shed for many for the remission of sins. The Testament says the salvation is for the Gentiles and for the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and the Gentiles named beside Yashar'el (Israel) are the scattered seed of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) living among the nations, which is why the news goes out broadly: the sheep are scattered everywhere, and the ones who hear are the ones it was always for.

4869.new_note: *And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;* (Matthew 27:51). *And I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from thence the veil, and the holy ark, and the mercy-seat, and the two tables, and the holy raiment of the priests, and the altar of incense, and the forty-eight precious stones, wherewith the priest was adorned and all the holy vessels of the tabernacle.* (2 Baruch 6:7). The veil is torn from the top to the bottom, which is a tearing from above. In 2 Baruch the hand from above also acts upon the veil: the angel descends into the Holy of Holies and takes from there the veil, the ark, the mercy seat and every holy vessel, and the next verse in the book says he charges the earth to guard them until the last times so that strangers may not get possession of them. In neither is the house of Yahuah (God) simply done away with. In Baruch its holy things are kept to be restored, and in Matthew the veil is opened from above, and the way back into the holiest is the way home.

Levi vision had named at the wisdom-stream-register the King walks-out at the incarnation-and-cross substance. The wisdom-stream and the gospel cohere at the temple-fulfillment architecture.

4872.new_note: *And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,* (Matthew 27:52) *And some of them shall be high priests, and judges, and scribes; For by their mouth shall the holy place be guarded.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 24:17) Levi is told that some of his seed will be high priests, judges and scribes, and that the holy place will be guarded by what they say. Matthew shows the saints who slept rising out of opened graves when Yahusha (Jesus) dies, which can be read as a foretaste of the resurrection of the faithful that is still ahead. The two meet on the same ground: the holy place and the faithful who served Yahuah (God) in it are not left to the grave.
4872.member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 24:17 — *For by their mouth shall the holy place be guarded.* The faithful dead who rise in Matthew 27:52 are the same covenant line Levi's vision speaks of.

4872.old_note: *And some of them shall be high priests, and judges, and scribes ; For by their mouth shall the holy place be guarded.* Testaments of the XII Patriarchs / Testament of Levi (Charles edition seq #15, verse 17; standard Test. Levi 4:17 at the chapter-conclusion) names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the *holy place guarded* substance in continuity with the *I come and sojourn* substance of seq #15 v.2. Levi vision named at the wisdom-stream-register the saints-arising substance carries at the historical-pivot. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture in the prefiguring-passage; the cross opens the door-home for the architecture to walk-out operative.

4884.new_note: *And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,* (Matthew 27:52). *But those who have been saved by their works, And to whom the law has been now a hope, And understanding an expectation, And wisdom a confidence, Shall wonders appear in their time. For they shall behold the world which is now invisible to them, And they shall behold the time which is now hidden from them:* (2 Baruch 51:7–8). Matthew says the graves were opened and many bodies of the saints which slept arose. Baruch speaks of people for whom the law was a hope, an understanding and a confidence, and says wonders will appear in their time and they will behold the world that is now invisible to them. These are people whose whole life was the Torah, and nothing here sets their works against the promise. It describes the covenant walk of those who kept the commandments, and the opened graves at the cross are the first glimpse of the seeing that is promised to them.
4884.member_note: 2 Baruch 51:7 — *to whom the law has been now a hope, And understanding an expectation, And wisdom a confidence.* Those for whom the law was a hope are promised sight of the invisible world, and Matthew shows the sleeping saints beginning to rise.
4884.reason: 'Saved by their works' read as the covenant walk of the Torah-keeping righteous (law as hope), not a works-against-faith statement; no merit doctrine. The old note spanned 51:7 and 51:8 and quoted a combined 'standard 51:1-8' form; I quote 51:7 and 51:8 in order. Old note's Charles seq #21 numbering is stale.

For they shall behold the world which is now invisible to them, And they shall behold the time which is now hidden from them.* 2 Baruch (Charles edition seq #21, verse 1; standard 2 Baruch 51:1-8) names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the saved-by-their-works-shall-behold-the-world-now-invisible substance — the apocalyptic-stream's resurrection-glory architecture. The framework reads the verse against Matt 27:52-53's *and the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose, and came out of the graves after his resurrection, and went into the holy city, and appeared unto many* — the saints-arising-and-appearing-in-the-holy-city substance is the historical-pivot-foretaste of the broader-architecture 2 Baruch 51 names: the faithful-righteous-shall-behold-the-world-now-invisible + shall-be-made-like-unto-the-angels + shall-be-equal-to-the-stars. The framework reads the saved-by-their-works language CAREFULLY — NOT the inherited-Reformation-merit-doctrine collapse; the framework reads works as the fruit-of-the-Spirit-internalized-Torah per Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 36:26-27 + Yirmeyahu (Jeremiah) 31:31-34 + James 2:14-26's *faith without works is dead*; the works are the Spirit-empowered-walking-in-the-Way the framework's *Grace, the Way, the New Heart, and the Mercy of Depart* exposition unfolds. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-resurrection-glory; the saints-arising-at-the-cross substance is the historical-foretaste.

4885.new_note: *And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.* (Matthew 27:35). *And the god of that world will stretch forth his hand against the Son, and they will crucify Him on a tree, and will slay Him not knowing who He is.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:14). The Ascension of Isaiah puts the weight where it belongs. The one who stretches out his hand against the Son is the god of that world, the adversary behind the deed, and those who carry it out do so not knowing who He is. Matthew then tells it as it happened, that they crucified him and divided his garments, in keeping with what the prophet had said. The tree is the place of the curse that falls on a people for breaking the covenant, and the Son took that curse on himself, so that the scattered might come home to the Torah, not away from it.
4885.member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 9:14 — *will stretch forth his hand against the Son, and they will crucify Him on a tree.* The deed is traced to the god of that world, and those who did it did not know who He was.
4885.reason: Old note's 'FRAMEWORK-MAJOR', S-number and Red Line references removed. Keeps the old note's point that the curse borne is the exile judgment and not the Torah; no other theology added.
4885.old_note: *And the god of that world will stretch forth his hand against the Son, and they will crucify Him on a tree, and will slay Him not knowing who He is.* Ascension of Isaiah 9:14 names THE direct external-witness verbal-anchor for the god-of-that-world-stretching-forth-his-hand-against-the-Son-and-they-will-crucify-Him-on-a-tree substance — the wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the world-rulers-and-their-rulers-not-knowing-who-the-Son-is at the heavenly-register. The framework reads the verse against Matt 27:35's *and they crucified him* — the operative-walking-out at the historical-pivot of the architecture Ascension of Isaiah had named centuries before at the wisdom-stream-witness. The framework reads the *not knowing who He is* substance in continuity with 1 Corinthians 2:8's *had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.* The framework reads the *crucify Him on a tree* substance in continuity with Devarim (Deuteronomy) 21:22-23 + Galatians 3:13's *cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree* — the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-the-curse-of-the-Deuteronomy-28-exile-judgment-substance the twelve-tribes-walked-substantively, as the Pesach (Passover)-lamb-substance, walking-out-the-substance the twelve-tribes-can-be-gathered-home-substantively per Red Line #4's reading (the curse is the exile-judgment, NOT the Torah; the King walks-the-curse, not the abolishing-of-the-Torah). Per Yoshi's S32 sourcing-decision (api/seed.py:EDITION_PROFILES["ascension-isaiah"]), AI is the *first witness* aligning with the framework's Formless-Father / Formed-of-the-Formless nature-of-God teaching — pre-Nicene, late-1st / early-2nd CE. FRAMEWORK-MAJOR.

4886.new_note: *Yahusha (Jesus), when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.* (Matthew 27:50). *And when He hath plundered the angel of death, He will ascend on the third day, and he will remain in that world five hundred and forty-five days.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:16). Matthew tells that Yahusha (Jesus) cried out and yielded up the ghost, and the verb is his own: he gave himself up. The Ascension of Isaiah says what that death was for. He goes down and plunders the angel of death, and on the third day he ascends. The death at the cross is the doorway of the descent, and the descent ends in the rising.
4886.member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 9:16 — *when He hath plundered the angel of death, He will ascend on the third day.* The Son who yielded up the ghost at the cross plunders the angel of death and rises on the third day.
4886.old_note: *And when He hath plundered the angel of death, He will ascend on the third day, and he will remain in that world five hundred and forty-five days.* Ascension of Isaiah 9:16 names the wisdom-stream's direct external-witness articulation of the plundered-angel-of-death-and-ascend-on-the-third-day substance — the architecture of the King's descent-into-death-and-resurrection-on-the-third-day at the wisdom-stream-register. The framework reads the verse against Matt 27:50's *Yahusha (Jesus), when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost* — the King's-voluntary-walking-into-death is the substance Ascension of Isaiah names as the descent-to-plunder-the-angel-of-death. The framework reads the verses in continuity with Hosheia (Hosea) 6:2's *after two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up* + Hosheia (Hosea) 13:14's *I will ransom them from the power of the grave* + 1 Peter 3:18-20's *put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit: by which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison* + Hebrews 2:14-15's *that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil; and deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.* The wisdom-stream and the apostolic-stream cohere at the descent-to-plunder-the-angel-of-death architecture per Red Line #11's reading.

4887.new_note: *And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,* (Matthew 27:52). *And then many of the righteous will ascend with Him, whose spirits do not receive their garments till Yahuah (Lord) Messiah (Christ) ascend and they ascend with Him.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:17). Matthew says the graves were opened and many bodies of the saints which slept arose. The Ascension of Isaiah says why the righteous waited as they did: their spirits do not receive their garments until the Messiah ascends, and then many of them ascend with him. Those who walked the covenant faithfully and slept are the first to be brought out when the way is opened, and the opened graves at the cross are a foretaste of the larger rising still to come.
4887.member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 9:17 — *many of the righteous will ascend with Him, whose spirits do not receive their garments.* The righteous who sleep wait for the Messiah's ascension, and Matthew shows the first of them rising.
4887.old_note: *And then many of the righteous will ascend with Him, whose spirits do not receive their garments till Yahuah (Lord) Messiah (Christ) ascend and they ascend with Him.* Ascension of Isaiah 9:17 names THE direct external-witness verbal-anchor for the *many of the righteous will ascend with Him* substance — the wisdom-stream's articulation of the architecture Matt 27:52-53 walks-out at the historical-pivot. The framework reads the verses together: AI 9:17 IS the operative external-witness verbal-anchor for *the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose, and came out of the graves after his resurrection, and went into the holy city, and appeared unto many* (Matt 27:52-53). The substance the gospel walks-out at the historical-cross-pivot is the substance Ascension of Isaiah had named at the wisdom-stream-register. The *whose spirits do not receive their garments till Yahuah (Lord) Messiah (Christ) ascend and they ascend with Him* substance reads in continuity with Hebrews 11:39-40's *these all, having obtained a good report through faith, received not the promise: Yahuah (God) having provided some better thing for us, that they without us should not be made perfect* per Red Line #11. The forefathers-who-walked-the-covenant-faithfully Yahuah is able to graft-in-again at the first-resurrection (Romans 11:24); Matt 27:52-53 is the historical-foretaste of the broader-first-resurrection-at-the-King's-coming. FRAMEWORK-MAJOR.

4888.new_note: *And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.* (Matthew 27:35). *In Jerusalem indeed I saw Him being crucified on a tree:* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:20). Matthew tells of the crucifixion in a few plain lines and says it came to pass according to what was spoken by the prophet. The Ascension of Isaiah has Isaiah himself seeing it first, and naming the place: in Jerusalem, on a tree. What Matthew sets down as history, the prophet was shown beforehand.
4888.member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:20 — *In Jerusalem indeed I saw Him being crucified on a tree.* Isaiah is shown the crucifixion ahead of time, in Jerusalem, on a tree.
4888.old_note: *In Jerusalem indeed I saw Him being crucified on a tree.* Ascension of Isaiah 11:20 names the wisdom-stream's direct external-witness historical-attestation of the crucified-on-a-tree-in-Jerusalem substance — the prophet-Yeshayahu (Isaiah)-saw-in-vision what the King walked at the historical-pivot. The framework reads the verse against Matt 27:35's *and they crucified him* — the wisdom-stream had named the operative-substance at the prophet-Yeshayahu-register; the historical-pivot at the cross is the seeing-what-Yeshayahu-saw substance walking-out. The framework reads this in continuity with John 12:41's *these things said Esaias (Isaiah), when he saw his glory, and spake of him* — the prophet Yeshayahu (Isaiah) saw the King at multiple registers (the holy-holy-holy-vision of Yeshayahu 6, the Suffering-Servant of Yeshayahu 53, the Ascension-of-Isaiah-11-vision of the King's-Bethlehem-birth-and-cross). The cross walks-out the substance the prophet saw-in-vision centuries before.

4889.new_note: *And laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, and departed.* (Matthew 27:60). *And after this the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was, and they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:19). Matthew closes the day with the body laid in a new tomb cut in the rock and a great stone rolled to the door. The Ascension of Isaiah tells where the Beloved was while the body lay there: after they crucified Him, He descended to the angel of Sheol. The same verse says the adversary envied him and stirred up the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against him, not knowing who He was. The charge lies with the adversary who envied and stirred, and a people who did not know who they were handing over are the lost sheep, not enemies.
4889.member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:19 — *they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.* While the body lay in the sealed tomb, the Beloved went down to the angel of Sheol.

4889.old_note: *And after this the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was, and they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.* Ascension of Isaiah 11:19 names the wisdom-stream's direct external-witness articulation of the descended-to-the-angel-of-Sheol substance — the King's-burial-and-descent-into-the-place-of-the-dead architecture. The framework reads the verse against Matt 27:60's *and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, and departed* — the burial in Yoseph (Joseph) of Arimathea's rich-man's-tomb walks-out the Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 53:9's *he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death* substance AND is the historical-pivot of the descent-to-the-angel-of-Sheol architecture AI 11:19 names. The framework reads the substance carefully against Red Line #9 — the *roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him* substance reads in continuity with the framework's system-not-people posture per the four-costumes-and-their-victims architecture: the adversary-roused-the-leadership-of-the-second-Temple-aristocracy at the historical-pivot, NOT the substantial-Yahudah (Jewish)-people-as-a-whole; the framework rejects the inherited-Christian-replacement-theology weaponization of this verse against the Yahudim (Jews) as a people. The cross + the descent + the resurrection-on-the-third-day are the architecture the wisdom-stream named at the prophet-Yeshayahu-vision-register.

4894.new_note: *He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where Yahusha (Lord) lay.* (Matthew 28:6). *And likewise after the third day rise again and remain days.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:21). At the empty tomb the angel says that he is not here, for he is risen, as he said. The Ascension of Isaiah has Isaiah told the same in vision, that He will rise after the third day and remain days. The rising was not an afterthought, it was said before by Yahusha (Jesus) himself and seen before by the prophet, and the days he remained with his own after rising are the days the vision speaks of.
4894.member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:21 — *after the third day rise again and remain days.* Isaiah is shown the rising after the third day and the days He remained, which the angel at the tomb announces as fulfilled.
4894.reason: Old note named the forty days of Acts 1:3; I kept only a general sentence about the days He remained, since the live verse says only 'remain days'.

The framework reads the verse against Matt 28:6's *He is not here: for he is risen, as he said.* The heavenly-messenger's-announcement at the empty-tomb is the operative-fulfillment of the substance AI 11:21 had named at the wisdom-stream-vision-register centuries before — the third-day-rise-again-substance the prophet-Yeshayahu (Isaiah) had seen-in-vision walks the same architecture Hosea 6:2's *after two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up* names at the Tanakh-register and Jonah 1:17's three-days-and-three-nights names at the pre-figuration-register. The remain-days-substance ties to the forty-days-between-Resurrection-and-Ascension per Acts 1:3. FRAMEWORK-MAJOR.

4895.new_note: *Now when they were going, behold, some of the watch came into the city, and shewed unto the chief priests all the things that were done.* (Matthew 28:11). *And after this the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was, and they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:19). Matthew tells that some of the watch came into the city and showed the chief priests all that had been done, and the verses that follow tell of money given to the soldiers to carry a false story. The Ascension of Isaiah gives the order of it: the adversary envied him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against him, not knowing who He was. The line runs from the adversary through those who held the seat of leadership, and the many who were roused did not know, and are deceived sheep. It is a system that lied, and no verse here makes a whole people the enemy.
4895.member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:19 — *the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was.* The adversary roused the people not knowing who He was, and Matthew shows the leadership answering the truth with a cover story.

AI 11:19 names the architecture explicitly: the adversary (Sammael Satan per AI 11:41) is the substantial-source; the children-of-Yashar'el (Israel) are roused-against-Him not-knowing-who-He-was — the people-as-victims of-the-substantial-deception-the-leadership-handed-them. The chief-priests' bribery-cover-up at Matt 28:12-15 is the operative-form of the same architecture: the corrupt-leadership-system fabricating the anti-Resurrection-narrative and walking-it-out-into the broader-Yahudim (Jews)-community-substance. The substantial-system-not-people posture holds non-negotiable.

4896.new_note: *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):* (Matthew 28:19). *And the angel who conducted me said: "Understand, Isaiah": and I saw when He sent out the Twelve Apostles and ascended.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:22). Isaiah sees Him send out the Twelve Apostles and then ascend, and Matthew has the sending in his own words: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations. Twelve are sent because the twelve tribes are the ones being sought, and the nations are where the scattered of those tribes now live. We do not know the sheep by sight, so the word goes out broadly, and the sheep hear his voice.
4896.member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:22 — *I saw when He sent out the Twelve Apostles and ascended.* The sending of the Twelve and the ascension are seen together, as Matthew's last words to the Twelve are spoken.

The framework reads the verse against Matt 28:19's *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations* — the substantial-Great-Commission walks-OUT-FROM-Galilee-of-the-scattered-seed (per Matt 4:14-16 / Isaiah 9:1-2) INTO-the-territories-of-the-substantial-nations-substance the scattered-seed-of-both-houses is-substantively-among. The substantial-Twelve-Apostles substance walks the substantial-twelve-tribes-restoration-architecture-substance per Matt 19:28 (*ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)*) + Revelation 21:14 (the twelve-foundations-of-the-new-Yerushalayim (Jerusalem)) — the wisdom-stream had named the architecture; the gospel-substance names the operative-form. FRAMEWORK-MAJOR.

4897.new_note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* (Matthew 28:18). *And I saw how He ascended into the seventh heaven, and all the righteous and all the angels praised Him. And then I saw Him sit down on the right hand of that Great Glory whose glory I told you that I could not behold.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:32). The Ascension of Isaiah says He sat down on the right hand of that Great Glory whose glory the prophet could not behold. The Great Glory is the Father, the formless one, and the Son who took form sits at his right hand. When Yahusha (Jesus) says in Matthew that all power is given unto him in heaven and in earth, the word given tells the same story: the Son receives the power from the Father who gives it, and takes his seat beside him.
4897.member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 11:32 — *I saw Him sit down on the right hand of that Great Glory.* The Son sits at the right hand of the Great Glory, the Father, and Matthew has him say that all power is given unto him.

And then I saw Him sit down on the right hand of that Great Glory whose glory I told you that I could not behold.* Ascension of Isaiah 11:32 names THE direct external-witness verbal-anchor for the King's-Ascension-to-the-right-hand-of-the-Great-Glory substance — the operative-substance of Psalm 110:1's *Yahuah (the LORD) said unto my Adon (Lord), Sit thou at my right hand* the prophet-David walked at the Tanakh-register. The framework reads the verse against Matt 28:18's *All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* The substantial-Great-Glory at AI 11:32 is the Father — the Formless-Source per the framework's nature-of-God reading per Red Line #10; the substantial-right-hand-of-the-Great-Glory is the place from-which the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-the-Daniel-7:13-14 dominion-and-glory-and-a-kingdom-substance. The substantial-substance is the Father-Son-relational-architecture-substance — NOT-categorical-three-co-equal-persons-Trinitarian-substance the inherited-Christian-Nicene-Constantinople-collapse walks. The King's *all power is given unto me* names the Father-giving-the-Son the everlasting-dominion the prophet-Daniel walked at Daniel 7:14; AI 11:32 names the heavenly-vision-substance the gospel-substance enacts at the historical-pivot. The framework reads this in continuity with Philippians 2:9-11 (*Elohim (God) also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name*). FRAMEWORK-MAJOR.

4908.new_note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* (Matthew 28:18). *And He shall ascend from Hades and shall pass from earth into heaven. And I know how lowly He shall be upon earth, and how glorious in heaven.]* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 139:5). Benjamin says the one who comes will ascend from Hades and pass from earth into heaven, lowly on the earth and glorious in heaven. 4909.new_note: *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):* (Matthew 28:19). *For all these things they gave us for an inheritance, saying: Keep the commandments of Elohim (God), until Yahuah (Lord) shall reveal His salvation to all Gentiles.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:5). 8023.new_note: *Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.* (John 15:13). *And him that hath the grace of a good spirit he loveth as his own soul.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 134:5). Yahusha (Jesus) names the greatest love as laying down one's life for his friends. Benjamin teaches his sons the same love at its starting measure: the man with the grace of a good spirit loves his brother as his own soul. A man who loves another as his own soul has already begun to hold his own life loosely, and the Messiah (Christ) carries that love to its furthest end.

12949.new_note: *And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Yahuah Elohim (Lord God) Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come.* (Revelation 4:8). *And such was the appearance of their countenances, of a lion, of a man, of an ox, of an eagle: four heads were upon their bodies, so that the four creatures had sixteen faces; and each had six wings from their shoulders, and their sides, and their loins.* (Apocalypse of Abraham 18:4). The verse before gives their four faces: *And the first beast was like a lion, and the second beast like a calf, and the third beast had a face as a man, and the fourth beast was like a flying eagle.* (Revelation 4:7). 45631.new_note: *And Adam began to make more requests of Elohim (God). * ORIGINAL OF THE LORD'S PRAYER SAID TO BE USED ABOUT 150 YEARS BEFORE OUR Yahuah (God): Our Father, Who art in Heaven, be gracious unto us, O Yahuah (Lord) our Elohim (God), hallowed be Your Name, and let the remembrance of Thee be glorified Heaven above and upon earth here below. Let Your kingdom reign over us now and forever. The Holy Men of old said remit and forgive unto all men whatsoever they have done unto me. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil thing; for Thine is the kingdom and Thou shalt reign in glory forever and forevermore, AMEN.* (1 Adam and Eve 23:9). *And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.* (Matthew 6:13). Adam keeps asking Elohim (God) for more, and the prayer he prays ends on the same petitions Yahusha (Jesus) gives his disciples: do not lead us into temptation, deliver us from the evil, for the kingdom is Yours. The wording is not identical, since Adam's version says the evil thing and has a longer opening, but the shape is the same: a plea for rescue and a confession that the kingdom belongs to Yahuah (the Lord) alone. The first man prays it after the fall, and Matthew records the same cry for those who follow Yahusha (Jesus) now.

45772.new_note: *Then You drew a rib out of my side, and created it after my own likeness and image. Then I awoke; and when I saw her and knew who she was, I said, 'This is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh; from now on she shall be called woman.'* (1 Adam and Eve 34:14). *And Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) caused a deep sleep to fall upon him, and he slept, and He took for the woman one rib from amongst his ribs, and this rib was the origin of the woman from amongst his ribs, and He built up the flesh in its stead, and built the woman.* (Jubilees 3:5). Adam recalls that he slept, that a rib was drawn from his side, and that he woke to see the woman and name her. Jubilees tells the same event from the other side: Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) caused the deep sleep, took one rib, and built the woman from it. The two accounts agree on the sleep and the rib, and each says what the other leaves out: Adam speaks as the one who slept and woke, and Jubilees speaks of the hand that built her.

45776.new_note: *And if You had punished me as You said, with death, I should have died that very moment.* (1 Adam and Eve 34:11). *Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:* (Romans 5:12). Adam looks back on the day he ate and marvels that he was not struck dead on the spot, as the command had said he would be. Paul traces the same line: by one man sin entered into the world, and death came through sin. What Adam says of himself in his own telling, the apostle says of him for all who came after, that the death spoken over the tree reached everyone through the one who ate.

45823.new_note: *"O Adam, as to the fruit on the Tree of Life that you have asked for, I will not give it to you now, but only when the 5500 years are fulfilled. At that time I will give you fruit from the Tree of Life, and you will eat, and live forever, you, and Eve, and your righteous descendants.* (1 Adam and Eve 38:2). *And he lacked seventy years of one thousand years; for one thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens and therefore was it written concerning the tree of knowledge: “On the day that you eat thereof you will die.” For this reason he did not complete the years of this day; for he died during it.* (Jubilees 4:30). Elohim (God) tells Adam that the fruit of the Tree of Life is held back until the 5500 years are fulfilled, and then he and Eve and their righteous descendants will eat and live forever. Jubilees shows how the heavens count such spans: a thousand years are as one day, and Adam, lacking seventy years of a thousand, died within the day of the command about the tree. The long wait Adam is given is counted in these days of the heavens.

45824.new_note: *"O Adam, as to the fruit on the Tree of Life that you have asked for, I will not give it to you now, but only when the 5500 years are fulfilled. At that time I will give you fruit from the Tree of Life, and you will eat, and live forever, you, and Eve, and your righteous descendants.* (1 Adam and Eve 38:2). *But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with Yahuah (Lord) as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.* (2 Peter 3:8). Elohim (God) promises Adam the fruit of the Tree of Life only when the 5500 years are fulfilled, a span counted in thousands. Peter tells his beloved not to be ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with Yahuah (the Lord) as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day. That is the scale on which Elohim (God) speaks when He tells Adam to wait: what looks to Adam like a very long delay is a few days to the one who made him, and the promise is held to its appointed day.

45825.new_note: *"O Adam, as to the fruit on the Tree of Life that you have asked for, I will not give it to you now, but only when the 5500 years are fulfilled. 45948.new_note: *And they stood and prayed Elohim (God) to forgive them their sins, and then fell asleep under the summit of the mountain.* (1 Adam and Eve 47:6). *And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).* (Genesis 4:26). Adam and Eve stand and pray to Elohim (God) to forgive them, and then sleep under the mountain. Genesis marks the line of Seth, and the days of his son Enos, as the time when men began to call upon the name of Yahuah (the LORD). 45968.new_note: *But on the third day I shall rise again, and it shall be salvation to you, O Adam, and to your descendants, to believe in Me. But, O Adam, I will not bring you from under this rock until three days and three nights have passed."* (1 Adam and Eve 49:9). *And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures:* (1 Corinthians 15:4). The Word of Elohim (God) tells Adam that on the third day He will rise again, and that it will be salvation to Adam and to his descendants who believe in Him. 58216.new_note: *For that time is the consummation of that which is corruptible, And the beginning of that which is not corruptible. Therefore those things which were predicted shall belong to it: Therefore it is far away from evils, and near to those things which die not.* (2 Baruch 74:2–3) *And Elohim (God) shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.* (Revelation 21:4) John sees the same turning in Revelation. And Yahuah (Lord) shall judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, for their unrighteousness... And then shall He judge all the Gentiles...* (Testament of Benjamin 10:6-9). John sees *the dead, small and great, stand before Elohim (God)... and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works* (Revelation 20:12). Benjamin's *all men shall rise, some unto glory and some unto shame* is that standing of small and great: the rising first, then the judging.

177477.new_note: *'And' then shall ye see Enoch, Noah, and Shem, and Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, rising on the right hand in gladness. And Yahuah (Lord) shall judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, for their unrighteousness... And then shall He judge all the Gentiles...* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:6–9). Benjamin sets the rising in order: the fathers first, then the sons each over his tribe, and last *all men shall rise, some unto glory and some unto shame,* and then the judging. Revelation names that last hour: *the time of the dead, that they should be judged* (Revelation 11:18). The fathers and the tribes rise before; the rising of all men, to glory or to shame, comes at the time of the dead, when the one judgment is set.

177478.new_note: *And after these things shall Abraham and Isaac and Jacob arise unto life, and I and my brethren shall be chiefs of the tribes 'of Israel': Levi first, I the second, Joseph third, Benjamin fourth, Simeon fifth, Issachar sixth, and so all in order... And ye shall be the people of Yahuah (Lord), and have one tongue; And there shall be there no spirit of deceit of 'Beliar', For he shall be cast into the fire for ever. And they who have died in grief shall arise 'in joy', 'And they who were poor for Yahuah's (Lord's) sake shall be made rich,' And they who are put to death for Yahuah's (Lord's) sake shall awake 'to life'.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 60:1, 3–4). John sees *the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Yahusha (Jesus)... and they lived and reigned with Messiah (Christ) a thousand years* (Revelation 20:4). Judah's testament holds the same rising: the fathers *arise unto life,* the sons stand as *chiefs of the tribes* *all in order,* and *they who are put to death for Yahuah's (Lord's) sake shall awake 'to life'.* The first resurrection raises the fathers and the faithful slain into an ordered kingdom of the tribes, and the deceiver has no place among them, as John sees him shut in the pit *that he should deceive the nations no more* (Revelation 20:3), until his end in the fire.
177478.reason: 'And after these things shall Abraham and Isaac and Jacob arise unto life... and so all in order' is verbatim at the card's 60:1; only the stale 'Testament of Judah 25:1, 3-4' changed (Judah 25 is live 60; live 25:1 is an unrelated Levi verse). Verses 3-4 are not in the packet, so they are carried over on the shift of the whole chapter.
